did_you_know.text: Did you know? Hiram king of Tyre sent David cedar timber, stonemasons, and carpenters to build him a palace in Jerusalem.
Did you know? David understood that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and that his kingdom had been exalted for the sake of Israel.
Did you know? After settling in Jerusalem, David took more wives, and more sons and daughters were born to him there.
Did you know? Among David’s sons born in Jerusalem were Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon.
Did you know? The Philistines went out to fight David after hearing that he had been anointed king over all Israel, and they spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
Did you know? Before going into battle, David asked the LORD whether he should attack the Philistines, and he was told to go up and fight them.
Did you know? David named the place of victory Baal-perazim because he said that the LORD had burst through his enemies before him like a flood of water.
Did you know? After their defeat, the Philistines abandoned their gods, and David ordered that they be burned in the fire.
Did you know? In the second battle, the LORD commanded David not to attack the Philistines directly, but to circle around them and wait for the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees.
Did you know? David did exactly as the LORD commanded him, defeated the Philistine army from Gibeon to Gezer, and his fame spread throughout all the lands.
